# Full-text index build and ranked HTTP queries

Measured: 2026-10-23T19:07:19Z. Host: mariogk-dev (amd64, 46 logical CPUs). Go: go1.27.3. Commit: `a2140904a212af048813462c30b8f6008a5cc497`.

Native library: pinned combined FTS + encryption release `turso-native-v0.8.2-fts-contract1-20261023`, linux-x64 SHA-256 `efd5916aa9ee1eeaa04784813b08e250912ae25d89f8a92499a216c2711f3e8b`. All six repeats completed, with 768 measured ranked queries verified and no request retries. The earlier incomplete run is preserved in [2026-10-23-fts-partial.md](2026-10-23-fts-partial.md).

Local two-region test cluster (gru/sjc), Release, client and server on one host; other development work also shared the host; requests target gru. Test-only issuer and temporary database; no production credentials. HTTP serialization, network, server query and response reads are included. This is local API evidence, not OCI capacity. The existing host freezes query deadlines; production timeouts are not measured.

Each size has three independent fresh collections, populated before timing index creation (`kind:text`, `fields:[article.body]`). Documents contain integer `n` and nested `article.body`: 32 words, 129 evenly distributed alphabetic topic tokens, one or four topic occurrences (alternating groups), and orchard filler. Bytes are the summed uncompressed UTF-8 document JSON sizes; HTTP envelopes and index storage are excluded.

One unmeasured disjoint-term query verifies the complete matching ID set and strict frequency ranking. Each repeat measures 128 different search terms exactly once, limit 10, sorted by `$score` descending; no measured query is served from a previous identical query result. Every response must contain only expected distinct IDs and finite descending item scores, with high-frequency matches first. Throughput is sequential closed-loop successful queries / elapsed time, including client correctness checks; it is not maximum concurrent throughput. Latencies exclude those checks. No request retries.

Only completed repeats appear below. A successful command must produce repeats 1–3 for every requested size.
